newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower - dealer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower - dealer.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by light packer demand and an apparent abundance of hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $53.50 to $54.00. Illinois top prices at the plant could range from $52.00 to $52.50.
Indiana and Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could range from $52.50 to $53.00.
Hog marketings were spotty Monday, depending on where harvesting was delayed by wet weather, the dealers said.

Eastern Iowa and southern Minnesota marketings were heavy following rainfall overnight and early Monday, sources there said. Some packers in the area indicated they had Tuesday's slaughter inventory bought by midday.

Prices also were pressured by sluggish pork demand, sources noted. Carlot pork prices at midday were quoted steady to $1.00 per cwt lower for hams, steady for pork bellies and steady to $1.00 lower for lean trimmings, USDA reported. There were 15.5 fabricated pork loads and 5.0 loads of trimmings sold, USDA said.
